analysis: Overnight macro dominates everything: the failed Iran proposal turned oil into the market's single factor, pushing Brent up ~3% and dragging 10Y yields to fresh multi-decade highs near 5.22%. Futures are pricing that through rate expectations, not geopolitics alone, with a 70% chance of an October hike now priced. That is a hawkish repricing that hurts duration and non-yielding assets, which is why tech futures are leading the decline. Company news is secondary today but not noise: Nvidia's agent-safety platform is a genuine new product with 100+ launch customers including Microsoft, timed to a real industry pain point (the Hugging Face breach and disclosed agent breakouts at OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta/Google). The Senate letters to Meta, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft add a political overhang on AI tax breaks but are an information request with an Oct 12 deadline, not an enforcement action. The Sino-US tariff relief is real but dated and being crowded out by the oil story. For USAC, the Saturday downgrade and Friday's break below the 200-day moving average are sentiment-dampening carried context ahead of the Oct 5 TXSE listing switch. Signal: oil-yields-Fed repricing into PCE/jobs week. Noise: scattered conflicting premarket megacap mover flashes from thin wire aggregators.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to end the conflict over the weekend; crude jumped ~3% and 10Y yields hit fresh multi-decade highs near 5.22%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Oil spike rekindles inflation fears, pulling hike odds higher and pressuring equity valuations into the open.

headlines.headline: US futures point to a lower open: S&P 500 E-minis down ~0.49%, Dow down ~0.36%, Nasdaq 100 down ~0.98% at 5:42 a.m. ET; VIX futures down 2.23%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tech leads the decline as higher yields weigh on duration-sensitive megacaps ahead of the open.

headlines.headline: Markets now price a ~70% chance of a 25bp Fed rate HIKE at the October FOMC meeting, per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hawkish repricing of the Fed path is the main transmission channel from the oil spike into equities.

headlines.headline: WSJ reports Trump rejected a seven-day ceasefire proposal and told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, citing U.S. officials; Trump told Axios Sunday he still expects negotiators to keep talking this week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stalemate keeps Strait of Hormuz disruption risk priced in; the bombing-after-midterms claim is single-source WSJ, treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Nvidia launched its Open Agent Safety Platform (open-source OpenShell runtime plus Sentry watchdog on BlueField-4), saying it could have stopped the Hugging Face breach; 100+ companies using at launch including Microsoft. NVDA rose 1% after hours.
headlines.why_it_matters: New enterprise software product addressing a live industry problem (rogue AI agents); modest after-hours bid, not a multiple-expanding event.

headlines.headline: Senate Democrats (Warren, Smith, Merkley) sent letters Sunday night to the CEOs of Meta, Google, Amazon and Microsoft demanding details on AI tax deductions and lobbying under the 2025 tax law; responses due Oct 12.
headlines.why_it_matters: Political scrutiny overhang on AI spending, but this is an information request, not enforcement; near-term price impact likely limited.

headlines.headline: Britain's Competition Appeal Tribunal on Monday allowed part of a UK consumer lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to proceed over alleged restrictions on Apple product sales on Amazon's UK marketplace; the claim allowed is worth £289–306M including interest.
headlines.why_it_matters: Legal headline with modest relative scale; litigation risk is slow-moving and unlikely to drive the open.

headlines.headline: Sino-US summit last week cut tariffs on $60B of goods and extended the trade truce to January 10, a relief offset this morning by the oil story.
headlines.why_it_matters: Carried-forward trade relief; helps cap downside but is being crowded out by energy-driven rate fears.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Friday): S&P 500 +0.51%, Dow +0.93%, both indexes up for the week. Overnight: Nikkei 225 -0.73%, Shanghai Composite -1.67%; Europe's STOXX 600 +0.2-0.3%. Precious metal miners lagging premarket on higher yields; energy bid on crude.
market_snapshot.notes: Oil-driven selloff in futures; 10Y at highest since 2007 per Schwab Network. Brent ~$107-108 (+2-3%); Reuters cites ~$108-a-barrel after Trump's Iran rejection; WSJ cites Brent Nov $106.82 +2.4%.

usac.headline: Wall Street Zen downgraded USAC from buy to hold in a Saturday research note; on Friday shares crossed below the 200-day moving average ($27.12), trading as low as $25.25 and closing at $25.49.
usac.why_it_matters: Downgrade plus a technical break below the 200-day average is sentiment-dampening carried context; consensus remains Hold with a $29.50 target. NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer completes this week (TXSE trading starts Oct 5, ticker unchanged).
